Like all things in the U.S. legal system, Good Samaritan Laws are a complex issue. It generally boils down to the idea that you do not have a duty to stop and help if you are not trained to do so. If you're a paramedic, nurse, or doctor (I'm assuming you're not) you might be liable if you don't stop and help.

Of course, you're in a slightly different situation. Legally speaking, your best option would probably be calling for help and allowing your friend to make the call to refuse aid. That said, it'd take a really aggressive prosecutor to charge you with anything either way. I think.
